clue.text: Study quietly, tucking into promising dessert

indicators.note: one thing tucking into another is pushed inside it, so the study-and-quiet pair goes within the promising word

parts.note: a budding talent is a promising one
to read a subject is to study it
P (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A pupil revising in silence while eyeing a dessert that looks promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sounds like eating, which fits the dessert, but it is the container signal; P is the musical mark for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked pudding made from stale bread soaked in custard is a classic British sweet course.

clue.text: Large number working to support William I?

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece supports the upper, so this one comes after

parts.note: Bill is short for William
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A big number of staff are employed to prop up King William the First.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million is a very large number.

clue.text: Disease referred to in paper: go to …

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: An illness mentioned in a journal, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links into the next clue's surface but plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease of rye and other cereals.

clue.text: .. note cited: prepare for discovery

indicators.note: to prepare letters is to work them up into a new order

explanation.surface: A cited note heralds an impending discovery.
explanation.definitionFit: Detection is the act of finding out or uncovering something hidden.

clue.text: One who's gone to pot?

parts.note: gone to pot normally means declined, but here pot is cannabis, so this is a drug taker

explanation.surface: A person who has fallen into decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes drugs, such as cannabis, called pot.

clue.text: Scoffing, father turned up in dodgy club

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or club

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Dad appeared in a seedy nightclub, mocking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' means read from the bottom, so father reads backwards before going 'in' the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoffing means jeering, and derisive means expressing ridicule or contempt.

clue.text: Woman's endless routine

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: normal means usual or routine

explanation.surface: A woman stuck in an unending routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Rich and healthy — bother!

parts.note: well means in good health
a to-do is a fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Someone wealthy and fit exclaims in irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous or affluent.

clue.text: Sell cycle component on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: a pedal is part of a bicycle

explanation.surface: A broadcast advert offering a bicycle part for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To peddle goods is to hawk them, selling from place to place.

clue.text: Not heavily burdened, indeed runs a very long way

parts.note: carrying little weight means travelling light
yea is an old word for yes or indeed
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A traveller with little luggage really does cover a great distance.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance light travels in a year is an astronomical unit, so it stands for an enormous distance.

clue.text: Change course to back English magistrate

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the word for changing course is turned round

parts.note: to veer is to change course

explanation.surface: An English magistrate is urged to alter direction and retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' looks like supporting someone, but it signals reading the course change backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial duties, akin to a magistrate.

clue.text: Perfect viewpoint actor holds

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer inside them, spanning the join between them

explanation.surface: An actor maintains a flawless point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect is undamaged and whole, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Attacked when went to sea

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
to sail is to go to sea

explanation.surface: Someone was set upon at the moment they put out to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be assailed is to be set upon or assaulted, physically or verbally.

clue.text: Idiot from Ulster meeting another fool

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
a twit is a fool, another one besides the idiot

explanation.surface: An Ulster idiot runs into a second fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal synonyms for a foolish, silly person.

clue.text: Top drive from here, with child on posh motorway

parts.note: a golf tee is where the drive is played from
a tot is a small child
U means upper-class, posh
M is used for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: A top golfer drives off with a child on a smart motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective but means a spinning toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotum is a small spinning top with lettered sides, used like a die.

clue.text: Defeat and remove criminal purchasing business

indicators.note: purchasing means buying up, taking something in, so one piece holds the other
criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A crook is told to take away a firm he is buying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges REMOVE to OVERME, which holds CO.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to beat or conquer them.

clue.text: Communist getting reprimand: here's where one could see stars!

definitions.text: here's where one could see stars!

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
to carpet someone is to reprimand them

explanation.surface: A communist being told off sees stars from a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see stars' suggests being dazed, but here the stars are celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities walk a red carpet at premieres, so that is where film stars are seen.

clue.text: Reformed lag in prison could become churchgoer

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A former convict turns good in jail and starts going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges LAGIN to ANGLI; a lag is a British slang term for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Church of England, or another Anglican church, is a churchgoer of that denomination.

clue.text: Grand inclination, picking up stuff

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a leaning is a tendency or inclination

explanation.surface: A strong tendency towards collecting things.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleaning means gathering scraps left behind, such as grain after the harvest, or information bit by bit.

clue.text: Start on short incantation in any one of four books?

parts.note: go means start, as in ready, steady, go

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spell is a magic incantation

explanation.surface: Begin a brief magic formula found in any of four books of spells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops one L from SPELL, leaving SPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The four Gospels, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, are books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Overdrawn with debts — that's quite nasty

parts.note: OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: Being overdrawn and in debt is a rather unpleasant state.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful and repulsive, decidedly nasty.

clue.text: Treacherous person, exhausted, stabbed by queen

indicators.note: being stabbed means being pierced, so the queen goes into the other word

parts.note: spent means worn out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A worn-out traitor is knifed by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake in the grass, a serpent, is a sly treacherous person, as in Eden.

clue.text: Careless and crafty, accepting nothing new

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the crafty word holds the others

parts.note: sly means crafty or cunning
love is nil, nothing, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A sloppy but cunning person refuses anything fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' is LOVE, the tennis score of zero, not the usual O.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly describes untidy, slapdash work or appearance, done without care.

clue.text: Former partner, with rising skill, making more

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: An ex whose talent is growing is earning more.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than is usual.

clue.text: Plant more bananas

definitions.meaning: a climbing plant whose root yields a red dye
bananas is slang for crazy, so more bananas means crazier

explanation.surface: A plant that is even crazier than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a dye-yielding plant; the second is the comparative of mad, and bananas means mad.

clue.text: How to lie and not get caught

definitions.text: How to lie and not get caught

parts.words: How to lie and not get caught
parts.note: looks like advice on fibbing, but means how to lie still and stay hidden

explanation.surface: Advice on telling untruths without being found out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is an idiom meaning to stay hidden and motionless to avoid detection.

clue.text: Pop over border

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Father crosses the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is the lower part of a wall, often set off by a decorative rail or strip.

clue.text: Innocent returned: time to break out

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for innocent is read backwards

parts.note: pure means innocent or blameless

explanation.surface: A prisoner found innocent has been sent back, so it is time to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst forth suddenly, as a volcano or a rash does.

clue.text: Drink and chew noisily on a good 50 per cent of bone

parts.note: to champ is to munch loudly

indicators.note: half the letters of the word bone are taken, here its final pair

explanation.surface: A dog with a drink gnaws loudly at half a bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Tasty fish — cooked raw turbot in top of oven

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters have been worked over into a new form
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cookery note: raw turbot is cooked in the upper oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges RAWTURBOT with IN and O from 'top of oven'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rainbow trout is a popular freshwater game and table fish with a pink stripe.
